item.description: Running AI models on phones can reduce latency, protect some data and keep features working offline — but local hardware still imposes limits.

item.title: Wi‑Fi 7 Explained: What Actually Improves — and Who Will Notice
item.description: Wi‑Fi 7 promises more capacity and lower latency, but the biggest gains depend on compatible routers, clients and a network that is already fast enough to expose the difference.

item.title: Ransomware Response: What to Do in the First 60 Minutes
item.description: The first hour of a ransomware incident is about containment, evidence preservation and communication — not improvising a payment decision.

item.title: Passkeys in 2026: Why Passwords Are Finally Losing Ground
item.description: Passkeys replace shared secrets with cryptographic credentials tied to your devices. The result can be both easier logins and stronger resistance to phishing.

item.title: AI Agents Are Moving From Chatbots to Browsers — Here’s What Changes for Users
item.description: The next wave of AI is less about answering a prompt and more about navigating websites, comparing options and completing multi-step tasks. That shift creates new convenience — and new security questions.

item.title: Deepfake Detection: What Signals Still Work — and What Does Not
item.description: Visual glitches are becoming a weaker test for synthetic media. Provenance, context and independent verification are increasingly more useful than trying to spot a strange blink.

item.title: Handheld Gaming PCs: The Specs That Matter More Than the Marketing
item.description: Display resolution, power limits, battery size and software support often matter more than the fastest-looking processor name on the box.

item.title: AI PC Buyer’s Guide: NPU, GPU and Memory Explained Without the Hype
item.description: If you are buying a laptop for AI features, three components matter for different reasons. Knowing the difference can stop you paying for capability you will never use.

item.title: RAG Explained: Why AI Search Systems Need Retrieval
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation gives an AI model access to selected external information before it answers. The idea sounds simple, but implementation details determine whether it improves accuracy or merely adds more text.

item.title: eSIM Explained: Transfers, Travel and the Security Trade-offs
item.description: eSIM removes the plastic card, not the mobile identity. That changes how people switch phones, add travel plans and recover service after a device is lost.

item.title: USB‑C Charger Guide: Watts, Power Delivery and Cables Without the Confusion
item.description: The USB‑C connector looks universal, but charging speed depends on the charger, cable, device and the power profile they negotiate together.

item.title: Browser Privacy Settings Worth Changing Today
item.description: A few practical browser changes can reduce tracking and security exposure without making the web painful to use.

item.title: AI Startups: The Metrics Founders Should Track Before Chasing Growth
item.description: Usage alone can hide weak economics. AI products need to understand retention, inference cost, latency and the share of work users trust the system to complete.

item.title: OLED vs IPS for Laptops: The Display Trade-offs That Matter
item.description: OLED can deliver exceptional contrast and response times, while IPS remains strong for brightness consistency, longevity and value. The right choice depends on what you do all day.

item.title: Android Update Policies: What Buyers Should Check Before Choosing a Phone
item.description: Long software support can matter more than a minor camera upgrade. Buyers should separate operating-system upgrades, security patches and feature support.

item.title: Browser Extensions Can See More Than You Think. Check These Permissions
item.description: Extensions can be extremely useful, but broad permissions may expose browsing data and page contents. A five-minute audit reduces unnecessary access.

item.title: VRR Explained: Why Variable Refresh Rate Makes Games Feel Smoother
item.description: Variable refresh rate lets a display adapt to the frame rate produced by a game, reducing tearing and uneven motion when performance fluctuates.

item.title: Cloud Gaming Latency: Why Your Home Network Matters as Much as Internet Speed
item.description: Cloud gaming streams an interactive video feed while sending your inputs back to a remote machine. Bandwidth matters, but delay and consistency often matter more.

item.title: Burn Multiple Explained: A Simple Way to Test Whether Startup Growth Is Efficient
item.description: Growth can look impressive while consuming cash at an unsustainable rate. Burn multiple connects net cash burn to incremental recurring revenue.

item.title: Edge AI vs Cloud AI: Where the Workload Runs Changes the Product
item.description: Running AI locally can improve latency and privacy; running it in the cloud can unlock larger models and centralized updates. Many products will use both.
